subject: Midgard renewal: competitive bid and capacity proposal
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex@midgard.ai>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai; procurement@midgard.ai
Date: 2027-05-10T16:12:00Z
Subject: Renewal review and competing proposal

Jonas,

Quick heads-up from procurement: Midgard has received a formal commercial proposal from NebulaServe that offers roughly a 25% unit-price reduction for generation tokens and a 2x guarantee on burst capacity. They're asking us to respond with either a revised commercial offer or a proof that Redwood's performance and operational guarantees materially reduce their total cost of ownership.

We'd like to understand: can Redwood run a short benchmark focused on latency tail, token cost, and warm-cache behavior, and can you offer any short-term capacity guarantees for Q3 while we finalize renewal terms? Procurement wants options on the table by May 24.

Thanks,
Alex Morgan
Head of Platform Operations, Midgard AI
procurement@midgard.ai

---
Attachment: NebulaServe-proposal-summary.pdf (pdf stub)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morgan <alex@midgard.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-10T18:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal review and competing proposal

Alex — thanks for the flag and the timeline. We absolutely want to keep Midgard on Redwood and avoid a disruptive migration. High-level response:

- We can run a 30-day focused benchmark on your representative traffic (we'll mimic peak burst patterns and long-tail sequences).
- We can offer a temporary "capacity accelerator": guaranteed reserved burst pool for 90 days with defined performance SLOs and prioritized routing, plus a provisional pricing supplement for that period.
- We'll propose an adjusted renewal term that combines a modest term extension with a usage-based rebate tied to sustained throughput.

I'll loop in Marissa (your AE) and Rishi (engineering) to scope the benchmark and the engineering guardrails. I'll attach a provisional terms draft and a short benchmark plan so procurement can circulate to legal. If that sounds good, can you share a 48-hour sample of logs (anonymized) and a preferred contact for the benchmark run? We're aiming to deliver initial bench results within 10 business days.

Best,
Jonas Weber
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-midgard-provisional-accelerator-terms.pdf; midgard-benchmark-plan.md

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-11T09:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal review and competing proposal — internal

Marissa / Rishi — internal thread to align before we present:

Context: Midgard has a vendor coming in on price and burst promises. They want options by 5/24.

Proposed playbook:
- Offer a 90-day Capacity Accelerator (reserved burst pool) sized to match their top-quartile peaks; committed hourly pool with entitlement to immediate spike routing.
- Run a 30-day benchmark that reproduces their 48-hr log sample plus an injected 2x burst window. We'll measure p50/p95/p99 latency, kv-cache hit rate, and per-token effective cost.
- Commercial: move them to a 15-month term (vs 12) in exchange for a 6% rebate applied retroactively if they sustain >80% utilization of the burst pool for 60 of 90 days. Also propose an interim credit / exec sign-off if NebulaServe slips on latency.
- Legal: present provisional terms (attached) that make the accelerator time-boxed and reversible if performance doesn't meet SLO.

Risks/issues: if NebulaServe's price is much lower, procurement may push hard on baseline list price. Our leverage is operational continuity (routing fallbacks, audit logs, private deployment hooks) and the bench data.

Can Rishi confirm we can simulate their specified sequence lengths and that KV caching will be representative in the bench environment? Marissa — do you want me on the next call with procurement? I can take the SLA/exec credit conversation.

Jonas

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-11T09:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal review and competing proposal — internal

+1 on the playbook. I'll offer: 3% renewal credit + two guaranteed reserved-burst hours per day for 90 days (no-cost for the burst buffer), and we push the benchmark hard. I'll get Procurement's preferred legal reviewer and push the provisional terms through our legal redline fast-track.

I'll also prepare an exec escalation note in case Midgard signals they will pilot with NebulaServe. Put me on any procurement call after you land the benchmark scope.

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachment: AE-note-midgard-talking-points.txt

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morgan <alex@midgard.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-22T14:45:00Z
Subject: Proposed accelerator terms and benchmark results summary

Alex — appreciate your patience while we completed the benchmark. Summary and next steps below.

1) Benchmark summary (attached): Redwood ran a 10-business-day bench reproducing your 48-hour sample plus two 1-hour synthetic 2x bursts. Results: p95 latency improved by 18% vs NebulaServe's public numbers (measured on comparable hardware), p99 latency was stable and within our SLO, and KV cache hit rates indicate a 22% effective token-cost reduction vs cold-starts. Full figures in benchmark-summary-20270522.pdf.

2) Commercial proposal — Capacity Accelerator (90 days):
   - Reserved burst pool: 120 vGPU-hours/day reserved (scales with utilization)
   - Pricing: provisional uplift applied only to the reserved pool for 90 days; baseline rates unchanged for standard usage
   - Performance SLOs: p95 <= 220ms, p99 <= 450ms (details in attached provisional terms)
   - Rebate: Signed renewal to 15 months with an operational rebate: if Midgard sustains >80% utilization of the reserved pool for 60 of 90 days, a 6% rebate is applied to baseline usage for the first 12 months of the renewed term.

3) Risk mitigations: immediate routing fallback to a compatible quantized variant if warming is delayed; audit logs and perf traces retained for 180 days; priority escalation channel for platform incidents.

4) Next steps: we attached the provisional terms and the bench PDF. If Midgard wants to proceed, I can open a DocuSign envelope for the provisional 90-day accelerator and the 15-month renewal. We can also schedule a 30-minute walk-through of the bench results with your engineering and procurement teams this week.

Links: benchmark folder (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_midgard_benchmarks) | DocuSign (https://www.docusign.com/link/MID-2027-0867-sign)

If you'd like, Marissa will follow up on the commercial cadence and legal handoff. Happy to jump on a call.

Best,
Jonas Weber
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

Attachments: benchmark-summary-20270522.pdf; redwood-midgard-provisional-accelerator-terms.pdf
